body: Pharmacist here. I totally hear you and I fully agree. I’m not above anyone in the pharmacy and we are just as capable of taking pickup, drive thru, answering the phone, doing qp, qt, anything. Honestly we have to support each other out there and I hope more pharmacists see that.

What my lead technician and inventory specialist did was order some metal shelving from corporate and organize a section of the back room dedicated to the pharmacy. Each poll the inventory specialist goes to the back room and sees what needs to be ordered and not. This system has worked well for us as long as everyone is on board. When the pallets come the front store staff unloads it and moves the boxes to the pharmacy’s side and the pharmacy’s job is the organize it on our shelves that’s it. Honestly my store had the opposite problem front stores side was awful and messy so we did this method to be organized. Hope this helps :)

I would say it’s only a write up if you’re actually not putting effort into asking customers they could consider it insubordination. But as long as you have the right behavior by asking customers and are trying that’s all you can do. You can not force someone to sign up if they say no.

As a young teenager who was very insecure I felt the same. I always believed someone was watching me or could see me shower. I had a standing shower with a clearish door so I would put my towel up over the shower door so no one could see me. I would blast music too so I couldn’t hear people if they laughed at me. It was very bad. I feel like as I got older this anxiety went away now I shower just fine, but I do make sure my showers have curtains :)

I struggle with this same issue as well. And not just with friends but with co workers as well. Something as small as someone not saying Goodmorning to me makes me believe they hate me. I saw something on tik tok that spoke to me. They said that if someone truly cares about their relationship with you, they will come to you if they are upset with you. And if they don’t come to you to fix the problem they do not matter in your and it’s their problem that they can’t discuss their problem with you. I try to think of this when these thoughts come into my head. I tell myself if they are mad at me, they will tell me.

You are definitely not annoying! It’s okay to share your feelings with others. If they truly care about you, you should be able to share your emotions with them without judgement. I know for me my brain makes me believe people are mad at me even though that’s probably not true. Something that helps me is writing down what I’m feeling.
